instruction.name: vmod.wu
instruction.description: Compute the remainder of each unsigned 32-bit element in `a` divided by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr2, $r4

latencies.notes: vj -> result chain. Data-dependent: latency = 5 + 6*2 + 16*quotient_bits/32 = 17 + 2*floor(bits/4) for a 32-bit element. Min 11 with a zero dividend, max 33 at a full 32-bit unsigned quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes (and both 128-bit halves) are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate. Measured with divisor 1, where the quotient equals the dividend, so the chain holds its operand constant and needs no helper. The remainder comes from the same divider.

throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 4.50 at 0/1, max CPI 16.50 at 4294967295/1. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LSX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
